whatThePageStates: This page is a catalogue of the GuardDuty finding types that apply to Amazon EC2 resources. A short preamble says all findings here have a Resource Type of `Instance`, that severity and detail vary with Resource Role (target vs actor), and gives two caveats (instance details may be missing for terminated instances or cross-Region API calls; findings sourced from VPC flow logs do not support IPv6 traffic). A Topics list enumerates 40 finding types, and the body then gives one H2 section per finding type, each with a plain-language title, a Default severity line, a single Data source bullet (VPC flow logs or DNS logs), a description, optional notes, and remediation advice. There is no table, no support matrix, no Yes/No column, and no statement anywhere that any finding type, Region, or data source is unsupported. The only coverage-shaped assertion is: these 40 named finding types exist for EC2, each tied to one stated foundational data source.

features.statuses: 40 documented finding types, all present-only. Counting: the Topics bullet list has 40 entries; the body has 41 H2 headings, of which 40 are finding types and 1 is the trailing 'See also' section; 40 'Default severity:' lines; 40 'Data source:' bullets. 40 = 40 = 40 = 40, and 41 H2 - 1 'See also' = 40. There is no supported/not-supported split on this page: every row is an existence claim ('GuardDuty publishes this finding type for EC2'), so the correct read is 40 Yes, 0 No, 0 Partial. Nothing here is ever marked unsupported, so a 'No' bucket derived from this page would be fabricated. Two per-finding attributes do split, but neither is a coverage status: Default severity is 21 High + 14 Medium + 5 Low = 40 (with 4 sections adding a conditional escalation in prose, e.g. Low when the instance is the target and High when it is the actor), and Data source is 25 VPC flow logs + 15 DNS logs = 40.
features.scope: Data source. Every finding type carries exactly one stated foundational data source - VPC flow logs (25 findings) or DNS logs (15 findings) - so the claim unit is really (finding type, data source). The preamble adds one scoped exclusion that qualifies rather than removes coverage: findings that use VPC flow logs do not support IPv6 traffic, which conditions 25 of the 40 rows. Severity and Resource Role are further per-finding attributes but are not scopes of support.
features.reasoning: The axis is a list GuardDuty publishes about itself - its own finding-type identifiers such as Backdoor:EC2/C&CActivity.B - so it is a catalogue axis, and findingType is the exact vocabulary match. The unit of claim is one finding type, not one detection technique and not one data source: the Topics list, the H2 sections, the severity lines and the data-source bullets all agree at 40, which confirms the page's own granularity is the finding type. Rows do not collapse - each of the 40 headings names a distinct finding type string, with no duplicates and no multi-row treatment of a single type - so distinctTargets and collapse are omitted.

shouldNotExtract: The 'Notes' preamble block (terminated-instance caveat, IPv6 caveat) is a limitation note, not a coverage row. The 'Default severity: High/Medium/Low' lines are severity metadata, not support status - High is not 'Yes' and Low is not 'Partial'. The 'Data source:' bullets are per-finding attributes; they are 40 restatements of 2 values, not 40 data sources and not a data-source support matrix. The 'Remediation recommendations:' paragraph under every finding, and the repeated 'Remediating a potentially compromised Amazon EC2 instance' link, are advice. The italic H3 sentence under each H2 is a human-readable restatement of the same finding type, so it must not be counted as a second row. Inline notes about log4j threat-list fields, the guarddutyc2activityb.com test domain, port 389/1389 escalation, and Elasticsearch ports 9200/9300 are examples and field detail. The trailing 'See also' section - the optional Skills for AI coding assistants / Agent Toolkit CLI boilerplate - is navigation boilerplate and carries no coverage. The Topics list itself duplicates the body: count it OR the H2s, never both.
coverageDimensions: REGION: nothing. The page names no Region, no Region table, and no per-Region availability. The single word 'Region' appears once, in a caveat that instance details may be missing when an API call originated from an EC2 instance in a different Region - that is a data-completeness note, not a Region list. Any Region count taken from this page is fabricated. SERVICE: nothing enumerable. The page is scoped to one detecting service (Amazon GuardDuty) and one monitored service (Amazon EC2); it does not enumerate the services GuardDuty covers, and other GuardDuty finding-type pages hold the rest. A 'services covered' figure cannot come from here; the honest reading is 1 service in scope, not a coverage list. RESOURCE TYPE: essentially nothing. The preamble states these findings 'always have a Resource Type of Instance' - a single constant value, not an enumeration. That yields at most 1 resource type and is not a resource-type coverage matrix; there is no per-resource-type Yes/No anywhere. The only dimension this page genuinely supplies is the finding-type catalogue (40), with data source (2 values) as its secondary dimension.
trap: The biggest trap is double counting: the 40-item Topics list and the 40 H2 body sections are the same 40 finding types, so a parser that harvests both bullets and headings reports 80. The close second is counting the wrong axis - there are 40 'Data source:' bullets but only 2 distinct data sources, so a parser keyed on the bullet marker reports 40 data sources when the page names 2, and a parser that dedupes and reports '2' has silently swapped the finding-type axis for a dataSource axis. Runners-up: (a) inventing a No bucket - nothing on this page is marked unsupported, so any not-supported count above 0 is fabricated, and the IPv6 sentence is a qualifier on 25 rows, not an exclusion row; (b) reading Default severity as a tri-state support column and mapping High/Medium/Low onto Yes/Partial/No; (c) counting 41 by including the trailing 'See also' H2, or counting 80 by treating each finding's descriptive H3 sentence as its own row; (d) attributing a Region or resource-type figure to this page, which states neither; (e) treating the four prose severity-escalation sentences (target vs actor, port 389/1389, Elasticsearch 9200/9300) as extra finding types.
